title: Status Packet Decoder
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Serial Communication for Robotics
description: Click the bytes of a servo reply to see which field each one belongs to. Then classify six replies as a valid reading, a bad checksum, a servo-reported error or not a packet, by checking the header, length, checksum and error byte in order. Used in Chapter 4.

educational.topic: Status packets, the error byte and the checksum
learningObjectives: Classify six reply packets as a valid reading, a bad checksum, a servo-reported error or not a packet, with at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Name the fields of one concrete reply, then sort new replies into four classes with a fixed four-step check
keyQuestions: Which check do you make first, and why does the order matter?
Can a reply have a correct checksum and still be bad news?
commonMisconceptions: Any reply that starts with FF FF is valid
A non-zero error byte means the data is wrong
A wrong checksum can be ignored if the data looks plausible
assessmentOpportunities: Six committed classifications, one attempt each; 5 of 6 for mastery

controls.label: Byte boxes
controls.range: click a byte to see its field
